transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` argument and naming the return.
Attached the generated immutable pointer-range postcondition `slice_ptr_range_starts_at_slice(slice@, range)` directly to the executable target.
Preserved the Rust 1.96 target flow: `let start = self.as_ptr();`, `let end = unsafe { start.add(self.len()) };`, and `start..end`; the implicit receiver is the only source syntax adaptation.

Reused the accepted executable core::slice::as_ptr start-pointer model through a local wrapper and retained only the unsafe raw-pointer range-end computation as a named source-backed provenance/range boundary.
